summary: The public half of the investor walkthrough is ready: home, How it works, Find jobs with its sample job and the start form load in 0.1 to 0.2 s with no console errors, no broken images and no sideways scroll at 390 px over 48 timed loads. The other half cannot be shown truthfully on the live site: production has never sent a job to a company (0 sends, 0 introductions, 1 approved company), the only simulations belong to internal test jobs that companies may never see, and showing a real site's packet to an investor goes beyond what the site agreed to. The unmerged demo build (PR 1369) still applies cleanly but adds only invented quotes and counts and nothing for steps 3 to 7, so it should not be shown. Demo readiness is red today; it reaches amber in about a day with a hybrid walkthrough (live public pages plus a recorded run of the real loop on test data) and green only after one real, permissioned job runs end to end.

good_things.what: Public pages are fast and clean
good_things.why: 48 timed live loads: time to first byte 61-173 ms, heading visible 0.10-0.20 s (company sign-in page 0.9-1.4 s), zero console errors, zero failed requests, no sideways scroll at 390 px. Nothing to fix for the demo.

good_things.what: The sample job is honest and plays
good_things.why: Labelled 'Sample job' and 'Stock footage, not a live job', credited, licence on file, names the simulation and first look instead of faking them; the video reached readyState 4 and played 2.5 s within 2.6 s at both widths.

good_things.what: The real loop is tested end to end
good_things.why: The core-journey test runs the real handlers on emulators from start to introduction, follow-ups and withdrawal in 25 s; it is the best source for a recorded demo.

good_things.what: The site's job page leads with responses and Introduce us
good_things.why: Companies first, each answer by alias with the company's words and what would make an introduction possible; the button and its one sentence sit on the first screen at 1280 and 390.

good_things.what: Public copy is consistent and states no price
good_things.why: Home, How it works, Find jobs, Questions and the company page say the same three answers, 'Free for sites' and 'Nothing is charged today', from one file.

good_things.what: Internal test jobs cannot leak to companies
good_things.why: One marker, written once, refused first by the company predicate; it is why the demo cannot accidentally show test footage to a company.

good_things.what: The viewer fails with words, not a black screen
good_things.why: boot.js turns a refused or broken scene into one plain sentence and a way back.
